title: Weak Randomness and Timeout Asynchronous Interrupts
platform_conditions: Ruby 3.x standard library; MRI — SecureRandom draws from the OS CSPRNG, rand/Random are seeded MT19937, and Timeout.timeout raises asynchronously from a timer thread
security_mechanism: rand and Random are seeded PRNGs (MT19937) whose state is recoverable from observed outputs, so tokens, reset codes and keys drawn from them are predictable; SecureRandom reads the OS CSPRNG instead. Comparing authenticators with == short-circuits at the first differing byte, leaking a timing oracle that recovers the value byte by byte — a fixed-length constant-time comparison is required. Timeout.timeout raises its exception from a background timer thread at an arbitrary point inside the block, so a multi-step security operation (write temporary file then set permissions, debit then record, grant then persist) can be interrupted between steps, leaving half-applied state or a partially-open permission.

source_sink_clues.source: Token/key material generated by the application; authenticator values compared per request; timeouts wrapping security-relevant write operations.
source_sink_clues.sink: rand / Random.new feeding security values; == / != comparisons of tokens or MACs; Timeout.timeout wrapping multi-step security operations

tracking_guards: Require SecureRandom (hex/uuid/random_bytes) for all security values; require a fixed-length constant-time comparison helper for authenticators; require ensure blocks that roll back on Timeout::Error and idempotent, ordered operations inside any Timeout block.
not_candidate_when: rand feeds only non-security sampling or display, the compared values are non-secret configuration, or the Timeout-wrapped operation is an idempotent read with rollback handling that leaves no partial authorization state.
public_references: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/338.html
